identity.title: SAGE: A Unified Framework for Generalizable Object State Recognition with State-Action Graph Embedding

problem.claim: Recognize object physical states and their transformations in videos for structured video understanding and applications such as robotic manipulation.

gap.claim: Pretrained vision-language models struggle with nuanced dynamics and temporal context, while specialized frameworks may fail to generalize to unseen actions or objects.

contributions.claim: Introduces SAGE, a unified framework that decomposes physical states into fine-grained, language-described visual concepts shareable across objects and actions.
Constructs a State-Action Graph with Large Language Models and multimodally refines it using Vision-Language Models.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors characterize SAGE as a novel unified model of physical state transitions based on shareable language-described concepts.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments show SAGE significantly outperforms baselines and generalizes effectively to unseen objects and actions in open-world settings.
The authors report up to a 14.6% improvement over the prior state of the art on novel state recognition, using less than 5% of its inference time.

narrative_sequence.summary: Object-state and transformation recognition is presented as important for structured video understanding and robotics.
Existing pretrained and specialized approaches are described as weak on temporal dynamics or generalization to unseen entities.
SAGE models state transitions through shareable fine-grained language-described concepts and a State-Action Graph refined multimodally.
Experiments are reported to show strong baseline gains, open-world generalization, and a large accuracy–inference-time advantage.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a concrete generalization problem to a representation built from concepts intended to be shareable across objects and actions.

lessons.interpretation: A transferable framing is to align the proposed representation directly with the stated failure mode.
lessons.application: When targeting compositional generalization, define intermediate concepts whose reuse explicitly spans the unseen dimensions.
lessons.exception: This may be unsuitable when the target task depends on instance-specific details that cannot be abstracted safely.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, baseline identities, evaluation protocols, or statistical uncertainty.
The reported 14.6% gain and inference-time comparison lack metric definitions and hardware or implementation conditions.
